effect: The fibroblasts and their matrix formed living supporting tissue, completing that goal; the muscle branch remains.
reaction: It is useful to see tissue presented as both living cells and the material around them.
reason: The remaining goal calls for muscle-forming cells, and the timed skeletal-muscle conditions specify a route from the unspecialized descendants to muscle progenitors.
expectation: The separate descendants will develop into muscle progenitors.

reaction: The parallel with collagen gene expression is clear.
reason: Amino acids should let the muscle-lineage cells translate their muscle-protein messages, as they did in the fibroblast branch.
expectation: The cells will produce muscle proteins and advance toward being muscle-forming cells.

effect: The muscle-lineage cells made muscle proteins and became separate myoblasts, completing the remaining goal without yet forming mature fibres.
reaction: The distinction between muscle-forming cells and a mature fused fibre is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building living supporting tissue from fibroblasts and their matrix was worthwhile: it connected gene expression and secretion to the idea that tissue includes both cells and extracellular material.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second differentiation-and-translation sequence was somewhat repetitive after the fibroblast branch, although the comparison helped show how different messages produce different proteins.

surprise.text: The supporting matrix required extracellular processing and assembly after procollagen was produced inside the cells, rather than being complete upon translation.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though terms such as mesoderm, mesenchymal progenitors and myoblasts were not explained in the supplied chapter; the lineage routes were clearer as sequences than as anatomical concepts.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the separate myoblasts develop into mature muscle, since this chapter deliberately stops before fibre formation.
